title: Coordinated multi-GPU scheduler for tensor/pipeline parallelism and NCCL overlap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement and validate a scheduler in the serving runtime that coordinates tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) execution to maximize overlap between NCCL communication and GPU computation during inference. Scope includes prefill (KV population) and decode-phase scheduling, kernel selection hints for attention variants, and runtime heuristics for dynamic microbatching and NCCL stream management. This ticket covers design, prototype, performance validation on 4/8 A100/NVIDIA H100 setups, and a follow-up plan for production rollout.

Context: As models scale across TP/PP partitions, end-to-end inference latency and throughput depend heavily on the order of operations across devices. Our current runtime serializes prefill and decode stages per pipeline stage, causing suboptimal NCCL overlap and underutilized GPU compute. Attention kernel selection (fused qkv, rotary vs. sin-cos, flash attention paths) also changes compute/comm ratios and should inform scheduling decisions.

Success criteria: scheduler reduces 95th percentile latency by >=15% for long-context workloads (8k-32k) on 8xA100 compared to baseline, improves overall tokens/sec by >=20% for mixed-length traffic, and adds no more than 5% additional memory overhead. Must be compatible with existing model shard metadata and preserve deterministic outputs within acceptable numerical tolerance when fallbacks occur.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration into runtime with opt-in flag 'multi_gpu_overlap_v1'
Benchmarks: >=15% 95th latency reduction on 8xA100 for 16k prefill + 512 decode tokens synthetic workload
No correctness regressions: decoded tokens match baseline within floating point tolerance; unit tests added for KV sync correctness
Operational visibility: per-request timeline traces emitted to Console for prefill/decode/nccl phases
Backward compatibility: runs with existing checkpoint metadata; falls back to legacy scheduler if model lacks TP/PP annotations
investigation_notes: 2025-02-19: Spike - measured baseline on bench/inference-multi-gpu: 8xA100, 16k prefill + 256 decode -> 95th latency = 1420ms, tokens/sec = 210. Observed large NCCL all-reduce stalls during decode start.

2025-02-21: Profiling with nvprof/nvtx: decode kernels on PP stage 1 idle while PP stage 0 performs NCCL all-reduce for KV sync. Found NCCL operations running on default stream block compute kernels on same device when streams not configured for async overlap.

2025-02-24: Micro-prototypes: (a) explicit CUDA streams per NCCL op improved overlap in single-stage tests; (b) reordering prefill KV placements to populate local cache earlier reduced inter-stage NCCL size by 30% for certain layer placements.

2025-02-25: Attention kernel experiments: flash-attn path reduced per-layer compute time by 25% but increased instantaneous NCCL bandwidth demand during KV exchange because compute finished earlier and triggered bulk comms. Indicates scheduler must be kernel-aware.

2025-02-26: Evaluated two scheduler designs: "stream-forwarding" (aggressively overlapping NCCL with local compute using dedicated comm streams) and "microburst" (split decode batches into micro-tokens to spread NCCL). Stream-forwarding is simpler and better for long sequences; microburst helps tail latency for short decode windows.

2025-03-01: End-to-end perf: implemented stream-forwarding prototype in local branch eng/feat/multi-gpu-scheduler. On 8xA100, synthetic workload improved 95th latency from 1420ms -> 1110ms (22% drop), tokens/sec +33%. Memory overhead +3%.
decisions: Adopt hybrid approach: default scheduler = stream-forwarding with adaptive microburst fallback when traffic shows high short-tail decode patterns.
Introduce kernel metadata into model manifest: per-layer recommended attention kernel (flash/naive/fused-qkv) and an estimated compute/comm ratio to inform scheduling heuristics.
Use dedicated CUDA streams for NCCL comms and tag them with NVTX ranges so Console traces can attribute overlap. Do NOT rely on NCCL group to implicitly order on default stream.
Implement runtime heuristic that monitors moving-window decode latency and toggles microburst mode when 95th latency for decode falls outside SLA thresholds.
Keep feature behind runtime flag 'multi_gpu_overlap_v1' for staged rollout and safe rollback.
tradeoffs: Dedicated comm streams increase implementation complexity and require careful stream synchronization to avoid race conditions; chosen because overlap gains outweigh complexity for production SLAs.
Kernel-aware scheduling requires model manifests to include hints; this adds onboarding friction for custom models but can be auto-inferred for supported checkpoints.
Microburst mode improves latency tail at cost of slight throughput loss and increased kernel-launch overhead. Default remains stream-forwarding for throughput-critical workloads.
implementation_notes: Scheduler will live in runtime/scheduler/multi_gpu_scheduler.cc with a thin API used by executor to submit prefill and decode ops.
Kernel metadata schema: add keys 'attention_kernel' (string), 'compute_comm_ratio' (float-as-string) to model manifest JSON used by serving control plane.
Testing: extend bench harness to run mixed-length arrival patterns and a deterministic-mode that records NVTX timelines for CI regression checks.
next_steps: Complete PR with unit + integration tests: target merge into canary branch by 2025-03-07
Run full cluster experiments in perf lab (4x8 A100 nodes) 2025-03-09 -> record Console dashboards for SLA validation
Draft rollout plan: canary podset -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full. Monitor cost and tail latency for rollback triggers
Document kernel metadata inference script for model onboarding and add to model import flow
